headline: President Trump said he is not downplaying AI risks but called the push against AI and data centers a "SICK conspiracy", while OpenAI's Sam Altman said he would welcome a slower pace of AI progress.
score_reason: Lowered from 8 because the remarks are from Sunday 27 and Monday 28 Sep 2026, before the 2 Oct cutoff; the statements are on the record but no new rule is announced.
importance_line: What changed: the White House and a leading AI company chief are on the record with different answers on whether AI needs rules, which affects voters and lawmakers before the November elections, then AI companies, and the doubt is that these are statements and the article reports no new law or rule.
summary: ABC News reports that on Sunday 27 and Monday 28 Sep 2026 President Donald Trump said he would not downplay AI concerns but wrote that the only "guardrails" AI needs is "a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT", while OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said his company would welcome a slower pace and a federal safety framework. Vice President JD Vance said any regulation should be done "smartly" and that it feels "a bit of a Trojan horse" to see AI companies asking to be regulated.
